properties.title: EndoWorld-JEPA: Motion-Guided Global-Local Latent World Modeling for Endoscopic Video Representation Learning

membership.reason: EndoWorld-JEPA is a causal motion-conditioned global-local JEPA latent world model predicting future endoscopic latent states from optical-flow motion conditions.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L0 latent-predictive representation world model (WT_PROCEDURE, BP_COMPONENT).

properties.backbone: Visual encoder E_V + Optical Motion-guided (OM) module + Global/Local JEPA latent predictors

properties.flow: 6 endoscopic frames -> OM Farneback flow decomposition -> Global & Motion-Local JEPA latent prediction at t+5 -> downstream classification/segmentation/detection/phase adapters

properties.purpose: Self-supervised endoscopic video representation learning for polyp classification/segmentation/detection and surgical phase recognition.
properties.environment: Four retrospective endoscopic benchmarks (PolypDiag, CVC-12k, KUMC, Cholec80)

assertions.rationale: Visual encoder E_V producing CLS and patch embeddings plus temporal motion encoder E_M.
Complementary global and motion-local JEPA predictors forecast next latent states without pixel reconstruction.

Section 3.1 (Eq. 1) and Figure 2 explicitly implement global and motion-local latent states (g_t, l_t) plus a K=5-step causal motion history window A_t from 6 consecutive frames carried into the next-state transition W(g_t, l_t, A_t^{in}) -> (g_hat_{t+1}, l_hat_{t+1}) at x_{s_t+5}. Boundary: one-step pretraining transition only; no multi-step recursive rollout is implemented or evaluated.
Causal one-step latent transition prediction to t+5 conditioned on preceding motion.
Learned JEPA latent predictors conditioned on deterministic Farneback optical flow decomposition.
Transfer evaluated across four external endoscopic benchmarks: PolypDiag, CVC-12k, KUMC, Cholec80.
Predictions execute in global CLS and patch-weighted local representation spaces.

evidence_fragments.content: We present EndoWorld-JEPA, to our knowledge the first latent world-model pre-training framework designed for general-purpose endoscopic video representation learning. In place of recorded actions, calibrated poses, or robot kinematics, the model conditions prediction of the next latent state on motion observed up to the current state.

We pre-train a single checkpoint on unlabeled endoscopic video and evaluate its transfer on four downstream tasks—video classification, polyp segmentation, polyp detection, and surgical phase recognition—using the corresponding PolypDiag, CVC-12k, KUMC, and Cholec80 benchmarks, which respectively assess appearance recognition, dense delineation, object localization, and procedural progression.

[paraphrase (visual p.4)] Fig. 2: OM block computes Farneback dense optical flow over 6 frames (5 incoming flows), decomposes dominant displacement vs residual magnitude R_n, produces motion condition c_t and local-motion weight map M_t, and trains Global + Local JEPA predictors to predict latent states at x_{s_t+5} without pixel reconstruction.

EndoWorld-JEPA predicts the next sampled latent state from the current global and motion-local states together with the effective causal motion input available at that state: (ˆgt+1,ˆlt+1) =W(g t,l t,A int ),(1) whereg t andl t are the global and motion-local latent states of xst,A t contains theKmost recent standardized motion descriptors ending atx st, andWis the latent world model.

capability_assessments.rationale: Implements core latent world-model identity during pretraining (global/local latent states g_t, l_t with K=5 causal motion history A_t advanced by learned global/local JEPA predictors to t+5; Section 3.1 Eq. 1, Fig. 2), while empirical evaluation is restricted to frozen-backbone downstream representation transfer across four benchmarks (PolypDiag, CVC-12k, KUMC, Cholec80; Table 1) without standalone next-state rollout error reporting or recorded control actions (L0).

limitations: One-step latent-predictive representation learning from passive optical flow; no recorded robot/probe control actions.
Offline retrospective benchmark transfer only; no prospective clinical deployment.

legacy_cells.B: EndoWorld-JEPA: Motion-Guided Global-Local Latent World Modeling for Endoscopic Video Representation Learning
legacy_cells.C: Jie Wang; Shilong Yang; Tao Zhou; Juan Yu; Rong Qu; Jianfeng Ren; Zhicheng Zhang; Linlin Shen
legacy_cells.O: Endoscopic video, including colorectal polyp and surgical-procedure scenes
legacy_cells.S: Do motion-conditioned latent representations transfer to video classification, polyp segmentation and detection, and surgical-phase recognition?
legacy_cells.AI: RGB endoscopic video frames; dense optical flow derived from adjacent frames
legacy_cells.AJ: ViT-Base visual encoder (patch size 14, hidden dimension 768); optical-motion encoder with 1×1 channel projection and two-layer SiLU MLP; separate global and motion-local transformer predictors
legacy_cells.AL: Joint-embedding next-latent prediction with global and auxiliary local mean-squared losses plus SIGReg distributional regularization
legacy_cells.AM: Shared visual encoder; a learned motion encoder maps ordered optical-flow descriptors to a condition token that modulates both latent predictors; residual-flow map weights patch pooling for the local state
legacy_cells.AN: Episode-prefix motion descriptors and residual maps are zero-padded; training randomly drops the complete past-motion window
legacy_cells.AT: None; current and target frames are encoded independently, with no prior-state filtering/update
legacy_cells.BL: K = 5 adjacent observation transitions per prediction interval (target five observation steps ahead)
legacy_cells.BS: Predicted next global and motion-local latent states; no pixel/voxel observation decoder
legacy_cells.BT: Video classification; polyp segmentation; polyp detection; surgical phase recognition
legacy_cells.BV: L = Lglobal + λL·Llocal + λSIG·LSIGReg; Lglobal and Llocal are mean-squared next-latent prediction losses, and SIGReg regularizes global states
legacy_cells.DN: HyperKvasir Video; Kvasir-Capsule; LDPolypVideo; PolypDiag; CVC-12k; KUMC; Cholec80
legacy_cells.DQ: Pre-training corpus: 6.44 million frames from 587 videos; downstream partitions include 173 PolypDiag training and 80 validation videos, 401 CVC-12k training and 171 evaluation frames, 15,578 KUMC training and 4,254 validation frames, and 85,984 Cholec80 training and 97,874 test windows
legacy_cells.DX: No next-latent fidelity metric is reported; reported results are downstream task metrics (PolypDiag video F1 98.3 ± 0.3%; CVC-12k Dice 87.2 ± 0.6%; KUMC F1 95.2 ± 0.9%; Cholec80 accuracy 89.7 ± 6.3%)
legacy_cells.EI: Against the strongest prior values, EndoWorld-JEPA reports gains of 2.0 points (video classification), 1.8 (segmentation), 2.7 (detection), and 3.6 (phase recognition).
legacy_cells.EK: Ablations remove or combine temporal conditioning, motion-local prediction, mixed pooling, and motion-window dropout; controls shuffle motion windows or use dense-flow magnitude only.
legacy_cells.EL: Optical-flow limitations/failure modes stated: rapid motion, large occlusion, weak texture, smoke, severe illumination change; residual responses may also reflect specularities, instruments, or flow errors.
legacy_cells.FB: Two continuous 768-dimensional latent states: a global frame state and a motion-local state formed by weighted pooling of patch tokens.
legacy_cells.FL: RGB frame → shared ViT-Base patch/CLS embeddings → global CLS state and motion-weighted local patch state; an optical-motion module encodes the ordered past-flow window, conditioning separate one-step global and local JEPA predictors; downstream task-specific heads decode classification, segmentation, detection, or phase labels; no planner.
legacy_cells.FM: Introduces EndoWorld-JEPA, which derives a causal temporal condition and local-motion cue from passive optical flow and trains complementary global/local latent-state predictors with mixed motion pooling and past-motion-window dropout.
legacy_cells.FN: A common checkpoint reports 98.3 ± 0.3% video F1, 87.2 ± 0.6% Dice, 95.2 ± 0.9% detection F1, and 89.7 ± 6.3% phase accuracy; it has the highest reported mean in all four tasks in Table 1.
legacy_cells.FO: Farneback flow degrades under rapid motion, occlusion, weak texture, smoke, and severe illumination change; median-flow subtraction cannot fully factor rotation, zoom, parallax, or multiple independently moving regions. The fixed K-step condition is one observation scale; long-horizon stability, uncertainty calibration, counterfactual control, and planning are outside the formulation; broader prospective and cross-institution/device/operator evaluation is needed.
legacy_cells.FP: Future work: confidence-aware flow, controlled temporal resampling, adaptive prediction horizons, synchronized kinematics, and prospective evaluation across acquisition rates, institutions, devices, operators, and acquisition conditions.
legacy_cells.FQ: Prior endoscopic pre-training treated observed dynamics implicitly; invariance may attenuate informative change and masked reconstruction models transitions indirectly, while standard action-conditioned world models assume unavailable controls or calibrated poses.
legacy_cells.FR: The paper trains one-step latent prediction but does not report next-state fidelity or multi-step rollouts; optical flow is an observed motion proxy, not a commanded intervention, and no causal identification, alternative-action counterfactual comparison, planner, clinical outcome, or prospective evaluation is demonstrated.

legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Expose the learned representation through a modality encoder/state interface, then independently validate next-state prediction before using it for simulation or control.
